q: What is the advantage of each reaction centre being served by hundreds of antenna pigment molecules?
options: Photons are caught over a wide area and funnelled in, so the reaction centre is excited far more often
Each antenna molecule produces its own excited electron, so hundreds of NADP+ are reduced per photon absorbed
It reduces the number of photons needed to split each water molecule from four all the way down to zero
It allows the reaction centre to keep working normally even though the reaction centre contains no chlorophyll
explanation: A single chlorophyll molecule absorbs only a few photons per second, even in bright light. By collecting energy from hundreds of antenna pigments via resonance transfer, the reaction centre receives energy fast enough to keep electron flow – and photosynthesis – running efficiently, especially in dim light.
